incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx + cross-region latency anomalies for eu-west -> us-west routes. alert_id=CRR-2026-34124. observed at 11:03 UTC.
Raj (oncall): Ack. Incoming pager. Taking ownership.
Raj (oncall): Quick metrics: eu-west->us-west p50 200ms->600ms, p95 up to 3.6s, 5xx increased ~15%. Traffic patterns show ~30% of EU requests are resolving to us-west-standby IPs (different ASNs).
Tom (network): Im seeing that the routing policy hasn't changed in control-plane. However, DNS answers from our authoritative cluster for host api.redwood.ai show multiple A records with unexpected standby IPs with relative low TTLs. Could be a bad DNS push.
Jen (dns): I pulled DNS change history: a manual override (change id dns-ovr-412) was applied at 10:59 UTC to include additional standby endpoints to broaden capacity during last week's maintenance; it was supposed to be behind a flag but pushed live by ops-assist. The override reduced TTLs to 60s but also propagated stale entries to some caches.
Omar (infra): Edge logs show a pattern: some upstream resolvers returned the new standby IPs and clients cached them beyond TTL due to downstream resolvers ignoring TTL updates. That caused a fraction of EU clients to bypass us-east/primary and hit cold us-west nodes.
Priya (sre): Customer impact: estimate ~15% of EU traffic to global endpoints saw increased errors and timeouts, mostly from interactive chat flows. Status page set to "degraded". SupportBot: creating incident INC-2026-34124 and pinging CS.
SupportBot: Notified top-20 EU customers with initial advisory.
Raj (oncall): Immediate mitigations: 1) emergency reduce authoritative TTL to 10s 2) remove standby IPs from answers 3) invalidate edge resolver caches where possible 4) pin routing at edge to preferred pools until DNS stabilizes. Ill take 1+2.
Jen (dns): Reducing TTL command:
```
# set TTL low to accelerate cache flush
nsupdate -k /etc/bind/key -v <<EOF
server dns-auth.redwood.ai
zone redwood.ai
update delete api.redwood.ai A
update add api.redwood.ai 10 A 54.23.11.12
send
EOF
```
Jen (dns): TTL set to 10s and standby IPs removed at 11:08 UTC. Waiting for propagation.
Tom (network): Pinning edge routes to us-east-primary pool to avoid client-side DNS variance:
```
rctl route update --src eu-west --dst global --backend us-east-primary --force --reason "incident: dns drift"
```
Tom (network): Pin applied at 11:09 UTC.
incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE: partial improvement detected by 11:13 UTC; 5xx trending down, p95 dropping but still elevated.
Raj (oncall): Noted some resolvers still returning standby IPs — likely negative caching or EDNS inconsistencies. Omar, can we push an edge resolver flush?
Omar (infra): Starting selective resolver flush and aggressive connection draining on standby nodes.
Omar (infra): Flush started at 11:15 UTC. Also ramping up warm pools in us-east for short-term capacity.
Priya (sre): Observed customer errors dropping. p95 at ~400ms by 11:20 UTC.
Jen (dns): Follow-up: found that a subset of ISP resolvers honored SOA MIN-TTL and ignored the updated TTL, holding onto records longer than 10s. Ill open a ticket with those providers, but short term we need additional routing mitigations.
Raj (oncall): Agreed. Tom, can we implement a short-lived HTTP redirect from standby IPs at edge to primary endpoints so clients hitting standby see a redirect rather than a 5xx?
Tom (network): We can add a redirect rule on the standby ELB to proxy to primary for known API paths. Applying now.
Tom (network): Redirect rule enabled at 11:22 UTC. Should convert hard errors to 200/302 flows while we finish DNS cleanup.
incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE: error rate back to near baseline and tail latency improving by 11:28 UTC.
Raj (oncall): Customer comms update: SupportBot, please send a post-incident note to the already notified customers with preliminary timeline and that service is restored. Mark for enterprise follow-up.
SupportBot: Will do. Drafting message with impact window and mitigation steps.
Priya (sre): Root cause summary candidate: an accidental manual DNS override (dns-ovr-412) added standby IPs into the authoritative answers without proper feature-gating and caused a subset of resolvers to serve clients stale or alternate endpoints; combined with client/ISP resolver behavior, traffic was routed to cold standby nodes increasing 5xx and latency.
Omar (infra): Follow-ups: add preflight checks to DNS change pipeline, require two approvals for global DNS updates, add resolver-flush play in runbooks, and introduce a synthetic test that validates DNS-based failover paths.
Tom (network): Ill add an emergency traffic-shift play that proxies redirects on standby pools and a canary for DNS changes.
Jen (dns): Ill revert the manual override from ops-assist and make the change via feature flag with gradual rollout and canary measurements. Also adding docs on TTL expectations and ISP behavior.
Raj (oncall): Assigning postmortem owners: Jen (dns) and Tom (network). Please include timeline, impacted customers, metrics, and proposed compensations.
Legal: Please ensure customer messaging avoids implying data exposure. We advise "no data loss; impact limited to availability".
Priya (sre): Handoff: Raj will stay on for 20m for any hot follow-ups then hand to Priya for overnight monitoring.
Raj (oncall): Final summary for postmortem:
- Impact window: 11:03 - 11:28 UTC
- Impact: ~15% of EU global endpoint traffic affected with increased 5xx and p95 latency spikes up to 3.6s
- Mitigation: reduced TTL, removed standby IPs from DNS answers, pinned routes at edge, standby redirect/proxy, resolver flush and warm pool ramp
- Root cause: manual DNS override + client/ISP resolver caching behavior + lack of gating for DNS changes
- Follow-ups: DNS preflight, two-approval gating, edge redirect play, SDK guidance on DNS caching, customer comms
Priya (sre): Marking incident mitigated at 11:30 UTC. Will draft postmortem and attach graphs to INC-2026-34124.
SupportBot: Incident state -> mitigated. Metrics stable.
